# Editor Cart Architecture Map — `cart/editor/` ("Shitty Games")

## Overview / Shell composition

- **Entry:** `index.tsx` — `ThemeProvider` → `Router initialPath="/editor"` → single persistent `AppFrame` (`index.tsx:15-23`). The shell is mounted **once** under the Router (not swapped by `<Route>`), so chrome + authoring state survive the Editor↔Play round trip.
- **Route read:** `shell/AppFrame.tsx:92-93` — `const { path } = useRoute(); const playing = path === '/play';`
- **The big state machine** is a single `EditorState` object (`data/types.ts:401-512`) held in `AppFrame` `useState`, reduced by inline `setState` updaters and the central `runCommand` dispatcher (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:334`).
- **Body layout** (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:2646-2833`): `Chrome` (top) → then either `PlayRoute` (when `playing`, `:2656-2659`) or the editor body `C.HW_Body` containing, left-to-right: `LeftRail` (`:2663`), `LibraryPanel` content browser (`:2666`), `Workspace` center (`:2703`), `Inspector` right dock (`:2785`); below the body `BuildDock` bottom status bar (`:2819`); popovers/dialogs/`DropdownMenu` mounted late at root (`:2834-2898`).

`workspace.cls.ts` (96 KB) and `editor.cls.ts` define all `C.HW_*` / `C.ED_*` styled primitives used everywhere (e.g. `C.HW_Chrome`, `C.HW_MenuBar`, `C.HW_RightPanel`).

---

## 1. The menu bar (top chrome)

**File:** `shell/Chrome.tsx`. Renders `C.HW_Chrome` with brand "SHITTY GAMES" (`:38`), the menu bar, a Compile pill, `RouteToggle`, and window controls.

**Menu bar rendering** (`shell/Chrome.tsx:40-50`): maps over `MENUS` and renders one `C.HW_MenuItem`/`C.HW_MenuItemOn` per top-level menu; each fires `props.onMenu(menu)`. `onMenu` is wired in `AppFrame` at `shell/AppFrame.tsx:2652`:
```
onMenu={guarded((menu) => setState(prev => ({ ...prev, actionMenu: menu, openMenu: prev.openMenu === menu ? null : menu })))}
```
So `state.openMenu` drives which dropdown is shown.

**The command registry / menu data model — `data/commands.ts`** (this is the source-of-truth). Key structures:

- `MENUS: Menu[]` — the top-level menu order (`data/commands.ts:11`): `['File','Edit','View','Map','Build','Story','Window','Help']`. The `Menu` union type is `data/types.ts:20`.
- `COMMANDS: Command[]` — the flat command table (`data/commands.ts:82-198`). Each `Command` (`data/types.ts:93-118`) declares `id, menu, name, icon, key, scope ('global'|'world'|'model'|'material'), available?, needsSelection?, submenu?, tool?`.
- `MENU_TREE: Record<Menu, MenuNode[]>` — the **nested tree the dropdown renders** (`data/commands.ts:317-343`). A `MenuNode` (`data/commands.ts:294-297`) is one of `{kind:'cmd', id}` | `{kind:'section', label}` | `{kind:'sub', id, label, icon, scope, children}`. Helpers `cmd()` / `section()` at `:299-300`.
- `menuNodes(menu)` returns the tree for a menu (`:345-347`); `commandById(id)` resolves a command (`:423-432`); `commandEnabled(cmd, state)` is the grayed-with-reason gate (`:262-288`); `submenuEnabled(scope, state)` (`:350-352`).

**Dropdown rendering — `shell/DropdownMenu.tsx`**: `renderNodes` recursively renders `section` headers, `CommandRow` (`:28-49`, dispatches via `onCommand(command.id,'menu')` at `:42`), and inline-expandable `sub` flyouts with an `openSubs` Set (`:54-59`, `:84-94`). Reads `menuNodes(state.openMenu)` at `:101`.

**Dispatch path:** menu row → `onCommand(id,'menu')` → `runCommand` (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:2896` passes `onCommand={runCommand}`) → the big `if`-ladder in `runCommand` (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:334-...`).

### Pattern to add a NEW top-level menu (e.g. a "Globals" menu)

1. Add `'Globals'` to the `Menu` union — `data/types.ts:20`.
2. Add `'Globals'` to `MENUS` array — `data/commands.ts:11` (position determines bar order; the dropdown left-offset is auto-computed by `menuDropdownLeft`/`menuItemWidth`, `data/commands.ts:434-446`).
3. Declare `Command` entries in `COMMANDS` with `menu:'Globals'` and a `scope` — `data/commands.ts:82-198`. Set `available:false` if not wired yet (renders grayed-with-reason).
4. Add a `MENU_TREE.Globals: MenuNode[]` entry listing `cmd('...')`/`section('...')`/`{kind:'sub',...}` nodes — `data/commands.ts:317-343`.
5. Handle the new command ids inside `runCommand` — add an `if (command.id === 'my-global-cmd') { ... }` branch (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:334`+). Toggling a root popover/dialog follows the `toggle-eventbus` pattern (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:643-658`).

No changes to `Chrome.tsx` or `DropdownMenu.tsx` are needed — they are fully data-driven off `MENUS` and `MENU_TREE`.

---

## 2. The tab system ("Editor | Play" toggle + workspace tabs)

Two distinct concepts:

**(a) Editor/Play route toggle** — `RouteToggle.tsx`. Lives inline in the Chrome row (`Chrome.tsx:59`). Uses `useNavigate`/`useRoute` and `nav.push('/editor')` / `nav.push('/play')` (`RouteToggle.tsx:19-20`). This is a router-level switch, NOT a workspace tab.

**(b) Workspace documents (the center-stage tabs)** — the real "tab/workspace" model:

- **Type:** `WorkspaceDocument` (`data/types.ts:56-62`): `{ id, kind, title, subtitle?, sourceId? }`. `WorkspaceDocumentKind = 'world' | 'model' | 'material'` (`data/types.ts:55`) — these are the three tab **kinds**:
  - `world` — the bird's-eye world editor (WorldEditorSurface)
  - `model` — the mesh/model editor (ModelDocumentSurface — vertex/edge/face/paint editing)
  - `material` — the Color Studio / material focus (MaterialFocusSurface)
- **State slices** (`data/types.ts:453-454`): `workspaceDocuments: WorkspaceDocument[]` and `activeWorkspaceDocumentId: string`.
- **Initial state** (`data/initialState.ts:108-109`): starts with `[WORLD_DOCUMENT]`, active = `WORLD_DOCUMENT_ID`. The world tab is permanent (never closeable).
- **Document factories — `data/documents.ts`**: `WORLD_DOCUMENT` const (`:5-10`), `modelDocument(model)` (`:12-23`), `materialDocument(asset)` (`:25-33`), and `upsertDocument(documents, next)` (`:35-39`) — the add-or-replace helper.

**Tab strip UI — `stage/StageTabs.tsx`**: renders the world tab as a globe icon (permanent, `:16-23`), other docs as closeable tabs with title+subtitle (`:24-40`). Rendered from `Stage` at `stage/Stage.tsx:120-125`, with titles DERIVED live from the model (`stage/Stage.tsx:61-65`).

**What renders in the center stage** — `stage/Stage.tsx:47-118` picks by `activeDocument.kind`:
- `kind==='world'` → `<WorldEditorSurface>` (`:70-83`)
- `kind==='model'` → `<ModelDocumentSurface>` (`:84-91`)
- else (`material`) → `<MaterialFocusSurface>` (`:92-110`)

`Workspace` (`stage/Workspace.tsx`) is a thin wrapper: `<ToolOptions>` (action bar) + `<Stage>` (`:51-56`).

**How to open a NEW tab programmatically** — the universal pattern (used ~8 places in AppFrame):
```
setState(prev => ({
  ...prev,
  workspaceDocuments: upsertDocument(prev.workspaceDocuments, doc),
  activeWorkspaceDocumentId: doc.id,
}))
```
Example call sites: `openModelDocument` (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:2323-2337`), `open-color-studio` material doc (`:702-711`), `createNewMeshDocument` (`:1534`), `createPlayerModelDocument` (`:1566`). Switching tabs: `selectWorkspaceDocument` (`:2457-2472`); closing: `closeWorkspaceDocument` (`:2502-2516`, refuses to close the world tab). To add a **new tab kind**, you'd extend `WorkspaceDocumentKind` (`data/types.ts:55`), add a factory in `data/documents.ts`, and add a branch in `stage/Stage.tsx:47-118`.

---

## 3. The focus panel (right dock — the "WORLD / No piece / BUILD / pick a piece…" panel)

**This is the `Inspector`, not `BuildDock`.** Note: `shell/BuildDock.tsx` is actually the **bottom status bar** (POS/GRID/BUS/UNDO/FPS/MEM telemetry, `BuildDock.tsx:83-152`), rendered below the body (`AppFrame.tsx:2819-2833`) — despite the name it is not the right dock.

**Right dock = `inspector/Inspector.tsx`**, rendered at `shell/AppFrame.tsx:2785-2817`, wrapped in `C.HW_RightPanel`.

**Content routing is by active document kind** (`inspector/Inspector.tsx:337-342` resolves `activeDocument`), branching:
- `activeDocument.kind === 'world'` → the **BUILD / PIECE FOCUS** panel (`Inspector.tsx:377-403`). The kicker text is `selectedPiece ? 'PIECE FOCUS' : 'BUILD'` (`:384`) and `<PieceBody>` (`inspector/PieceBody.tsx`) renders the "pick a piece…" empty state when nothing is armed/selected (`:389-398`). This is exactly the "WORLD / No piece / BUILD / pick a piece" panel.
- `activeModel` (model doc) → the **MODEL FOCUS** panel (`Inspector.tsx:405-493`): name field, save chip, `ShapeSection`, `RigSection`, `ModelOutliner`, `UvSection`, `PaintLayersSection`.
- else → a generic object/facts panel (`Inspector.tsx:495-555`).

**The right-edge pane rail:** `FocusRail` (`Inspector.tsx:291-304`) maps over `RIGHT_PANES` (`data/content.ts:19-25` — `inspector/layers/grid/mission/routes`), fires `onPane(pane)` → `setState({rightPane})` (`AppFrame.tsx:2790`). `state.rightPane` (`data/types.ts:455`) selects which sub-pane content shows (e.g. `showMission` at `Inspector.tsx:373`).

**Pattern to put a custom settings panel in the right dock:** the sections are just components composed inside the branch bodies (`ShapeSection`, `RigSection`, `MissionSection`, `PresetSection`, `ReadOnlySection` in `inspector/`). To add one: build a section component (see `inspector/RigSection.tsx` / `MissionSection.tsx` as templates), then either (a) render it inside an existing kind-branch in `Inspector.tsx`, or (b) add a new `RIGHT_PANES` entry (`data/content.ts:19-25`) + gate it on `state.rightPane === 'yourpane'` (mirroring `showMission`, `Inspector.tsx:373,539`). For a genuinely new dock branch keyed on a new tab kind, add an early `if (activeDocument?.kind === '...')` return like the world branch at `Inspector.tsx:377`.

---

## 4. The world viewport (bird's-eye 3D) + player / play-test capability

**`world/WorldViewport.tsx`** — a thin React pane over host doors. It renders the native `WorldLoader` primitive via `createElement('WorldLoader', {gameFile, storeDir, ...})` (`:658-664`); JS never touches a mesh. Spawned from `stage/WorldEditorSurface.tsx:62-75`, which passes a fresh, editor-owned game file: `EDITOR_GAME_FILE = 'zig-out/game/editor/world.gamefile'` (`WorldEditorSurface.tsx:13`) — deliberately NOT the `/play` route's file.

Responsibilities are all host-side via `globalThis.__compiled_world_*` doors (documented `WorldViewport.tsx:1-24`): camera (`__compiled_world_set_camera`, `:160-166`), live placed pieces (`__compiled_world_set_live_pieces`, `:256-285`), resident authored meshes (`:290-308`), map paint (`:248-253`), ground picking (`:341-359`). Camera is the cloned `IsoStage` (`world/isoStage.ts`), Sims-style iso.

**Pieces model — `world/pieces.ts`**: `PlacedPiece` / `ArmedPiece` / `PlacementGesture` types; `resolvePlacement`, `resolveRunPlacements`, `pieceInstanceRows`, `pickAuthoredPlacement`, `PIECE_MODULE_METERS`. Placed pieces live in `state.worldPieces` (`data/types.ts:472`).

**Player model — CAN be created and placed, but only as authored content, NOT embodied:**
- `model/playerStarter.ts` builds a **humanoid as a multi-part MESH document** (a data table of body parts/bones, `playerStarter.ts:1-18`, `:188` `playerStarterParts()`, `:240` `playerStarterSkeleton()`).
- Opened via File → New Mesh → "Player / NPC Model" (`data/commands.ts:41-44`, dispatched at `AppFrame.tsx:601-606` → `createPlayerModelDocument`, `:1566`). It opens as a **model tab** (mesh editor), not spawned into the world.
- To appear in the bird's-eye world, a model must be **Exported as a prop / build piece** (`File → Export`, `data/commands.ts:60-71`; handler `AppFrame.tsx:516-592`), which registers an `AuthoredBuildPiece` (`world/authoredRegistry.ts`) placeable like any other piece. So a player *model* can be placed as a static prop.

**No embodied player / play-test inside the /editor route.** The world viewport is strictly a bird's-eye authoring camera (iso, WASD-pan/orbit; no first/third-person avatar, no player controller). Play-testing is the **separate `/play` route** — `PlayRoute.tsx:17-24` mounts the host-native no-JS `WorldLoader` on `DEFAULT_GAME_FILE = 'zig-out/game/hmsc.gamefile'` (`:14`). The intended flow (comments `PlayRoute.tsx:1-11`, `RouteToggle.tsx:1-6`) is: edit on `/editor` → Compile (currently unwired, `compile-rle` `available:false`, `data/commands.ts:98`) → jump to `/play`. The `/editor` world file and the `/play` game file are different paths, and the Compile→Play bake is explicitly a future slice.

---

## 5. The event bus

**`data/editorEvents.ts`** — the editor's façade over the runtime `editorbus` door (`runtime/editorbus`, host-backed by `framework/events/editor_bus.zig`, durable SQLite, monotonic seq; degrades to in-process log). Comments `editorEvents.ts:1-11`.

- Event types are declared with `defineEventType<Payload>({type, undoable, describe, validate})`: `editorEdit` (`:58-62`), `piecePlace` (`:64-76`).
- Dispatch helpers: `dispatchEdit(h)` (`:81-86`), `draftPiecePlacementEvent`/`finalizePiecePlacementEvent`/`dispatchPiecePlacement` (`:93-154`). Callers in AppFrame import them (`shell/AppFrame.tsx:44`).
- New systems register their own typed events "through this same seam" (`editorEvents.ts:56-57`).
- `state.history` (`data/types.ts:460`) remains the local, capped, session-only display feed; the bus is the durable source of truth.

**`shell/EventBusPopover.tsx`** — the review UI. Subscribes via `onEvent(...)` (`:84`), reads the tail with `since`/`head` (`:86-87`), and **prefers the real bus but falls back to `state.history`** when the bus is empty (`:88-102`). Toggled from the Window menu (`toggle-eventbus`, `AppFrame.tsx:643-645`), the bottom dock BUS button (`BuildDock.tsx:104-108`), or hotkey Ctrl+H; rendered at `AppFrame.tsx:2834-2841`. Tests: `data/editorEvents.test.ts`.

---

## 6. World/global settings in the data model + persistence

**There is currently NO dedicated "world settings" / "global settings" object in `EditorState`.** The closest existing global/world-scoped fields (`data/types.ts:401-512`) are scattered: `floorIndex` (`:448`), `wallsDown` (`:451`), `viewMode` (`:452`), `snapIndex` (`:447`), `surfacePreset` (`:446`), `mapPaint` zones (`:511`), `worldPieces` (`:472`). A new `worldSettings` / `globals` slice would naturally be added to `EditorState` here.

**Persistence is split into three concerns (comments `data/persistView.ts:1-15`, `data/worldStore.ts:1-17`):**

1. **View state (hot-reload only)** — `data/persistView.ts`. Mirrors the whole `EditorState` into a Zig hotstate atom (`VIEW_HOT_KEY='editor:view:v1'`, `:21`) via `setHotState`/`getHotState`. `persistState` (`:72-74`), `loadPersistedState` (`:51-69`). Survives dev hot reload, resets on cold restart; transient overlays forced closed (`RESET_ON_RELOAD`, `:26-43`).

2. **World content (durable, on-disk micro-saves)** — `data/worldStore.ts`. Writes `WorldSave` `{version, seq, pieces, zones}` (`:25-32`) to `zig-out/game/editor/world-pieces.json` (`:23`). **Debounced micro-saves** (`SAVE_SETTLE_MS=400`, `scheduleWorldSave`, `:57-82`) — no Save button; every `worldPieces`/`zones` change schedules a write. Loaded once at boot and merged into state (`persistView.ts:52-58`). **This is where new per-project persisted world/global settings would naturally live** — either extend `WorldSave` (add fields + bump `version`, keeping the per-concern-file rule) or add a sibling file beside it (the codebase's stated "per-concern files, never one blob" convention, `worldStore.ts:13-14`).

3. **RMAP (the painting)** — the painted map is host-side, micro-saved to `zig-out/game/editor/painted-map.rmap` via `__map_set_autosave_file` (referenced `worldStore.ts:9-11`), reloaded host-side on boot.

**Model/asset persistence** is separate: on-disk package manifests are the source of truth (`ModelPackage.placeable`, `data/types.ts:314,343`; USER RULING req_2718). `cart.json` (`:1-7`) is only the cart descriptor (name, customChrome, 1536×940 window) — no project settings there. Authored placeables also cache in localstore (`data/initialState.ts:15-27`) but disk manifest wins (`bootAuthoredPieces`, `:40-51`).
